slides.title: Arithmetic Progressions
slides.speaker_notes: Welcome students. Sequences with a fixed step — APs — are everywhere from loans to stadium seats.

slides.title: What you'll be able to do
bullets: Recognise an AP and find its first term and common difference.
Apply the nth-term formula aₙ = a + (n − 1)d.
Recover (a, d) from any two terms.
Apply the sum formula Sₙ = n/2·[2a + (n − 1)d].
Insert arithmetic means between two numbers.
Translate uniform-step word problems into APs.
slides.speaker_notes: Read each; ask which seems hardest before starting.

slides.title: Sequence vs AP
bullets: Sequence: ordered list a₁, a₂, a₃, …
Standard form: a, a + d, a + 2d, …
slides.speaker_notes: Stress 'all consecutive differences must be equal'.

slides.title: AP — three classes by sign of d
bullets: Quick test: take ALL consecutive differences.
If any one differs, NOT an AP.

slides.title: The nth term — derivation
bullets: Memorise this — every problem uses it.
slides.speaker_notes: Walk through the derivation slowly the first time.

slides.title: Worked example — find a₁₀
slides.speaker_notes: Do this on the board step by step.

slides.title: Worked example — find n given aₙ
slides.speaker_notes: If n is not a positive integer, the value is NOT a term.

slides.title: Two-term recovery
bullets: Useful when (a, d) are not given.
slides.speaker_notes: This appears often in NIOS questions.

slides.title: Sum of n terms — derivation
bullets: Each pair sums to a + l.
slides.speaker_notes: Both forms are equivalent; use whichever is faster.

slides.title: Worked example — Sₙ
slides.speaker_notes: Watch the order of operations inside the bracket.

slides.title: Worked example — sum to a known last term
slides.speaker_notes: When l is given, the (a + l) form is faster.

slides.title: Arithmetic mean
bullets: AM of a and b is (a + b)/2.
a, AM, b is a 3-term AP.
slides.speaker_notes: Treat 'insert n AMs' as 'build an (n+2)-term AP'.

slides.title: Applications
bullets: Savings or production with constant step.
Identify (a, d, n); pick aₙ or Sₙ.

slides.title: Quick activity (5 min)
bullets: 4. Is 88 a term? If yes, which?

slides.title: Key takeaways
bullets: AP: consecutive differences all equal d.
aₙ = a + (n − 1)d — every term in one shot.
AM(a, b) = (a + b)/2; n means use d = (b − a)/(n + 1).
Word problems: find (a, d, n); apply aₙ or Sₙ.
Distribute the worksheet for further practice.
slides.speaker_notes: Remind: next chapter — Percentage and Its Applications.
